Unless you need to track fractions of a gallon, a uint32_t (which holds up to 4.2 billion) is perfect and avoids floating-point math overhead.
If you only care about whole numbers (0-100%), use an unsigned 8-bit integer (uint8_t). It uses just 1 byte of memory. If you need 99.5%, stick to float.
